scope: Engineering structural elevations. text2svg: parametric prose to SVG. svg2svg: existing SVG plus a natural-language edit to SVG. No JSON model is supplied in either arm; the model must derive or recover the geometry itself.

criteria.selection: Three completed non-truncated samples all showing the same substantive error. Truncated, errored and SVG-less attempts are excluded rather than counted as failures.

tasks.prompt:
Make a dimensioned structural elevation of the frame described below. This task concerns only the stated 2D frame, not complete product or building validation.
A 1-bay, 1-storey rigid-jointed plane steel frame, drawn as a structural centreline elevation. Column lines are spaced 3600 mm apart horizontally, starting at x = 0. Floor levels are spaced 3000 mm apart vertically, starting at y = 0 at the bases. Name the node on column line c at floor level f as N{c}_{f}, with column lines numbered from 0 at the left and floor levels from 0 at the bases. Name the column rising from floor f to floor f+1 on line c as col_{c}_{f}. Name the beam at floor level f spanning from column line c to line c+1 as beam_{c}_{f}. All sections are solid rectangles, b x h mm, with h in the frame plane and b out of plane. Columns rising from floor level 0 are 160 x 200 mm; every column above that is 140 x 180 mm at floor level 1, 140 x 160 mm at level 2, and so on, losing 20 mm of depth per level. Beams at floor level 1 are 140 x 260 mm, at level 2 are 140 x 240 mm, and so on, likewise losing 20 mm of depth per level. Young's modulus is 200000 N/mm^2 for every member. Every node at floor level 0 is a clamped base: both translations and the rotation are fixed. The idealised bases are clamped, not freely resting on a floor. Loads act only at nodes: at N0_1, 10500 N horizontal in +x together with -30000 N vertical; at N1_1, -43000 N vertical. No other loads act. Derived correctly this frame has exactly 4 nodes and 3 members. Report signed ux and uy at node N1_1.
Keep viewBox="0 0 1100 850". Map physical (x,y) mm to SVG (X,Y) as X=100+0.15*x, Y=610-0.15*y. Draw exactly the members of the frame, each as one visible straight element carrying data-member with its ID. Required dimensions are the physical centreline length of every member, tagged data-dimension="length_MEMBERID". Recompute every dimension and the analysis for the frame you draw. Report the peak extreme-fibre normal stress across member ends. Give at least three significant digits. Check against the limits stated in the task; make no other safety claim.
validation_techniques: FEM re-solve of the reconstructed drawn geometry
